name: Archival Map Investigation
description: An evidence-led investigative cover: one original subject or key artifact, a marked parchment map, and one archival detail strip beneath a precise model-rendered headline.
composition_guidance: Build an original evidence-led investigative cover. Pair one appropriate subject or defining artifact on the left with a parchment map in the upper-right and a narrow archival scene, document, or event strip below it. The frame should promise a careful explanation of how a concrete institution, agreement, route, or policy shaped an outcome.
composition_rules: Place one original subject or defining artifact in the left third; never reuse a real channel's crop, identity treatment, logo, or branding.
Place a weathered parchment map in the upper-right with only a few clear route arrows, dots, or boundary marks; preserve a clean visual hierarchy rather than a dense infographic.
Use a narrow lower-right archival detail strip showing a relevant setting or document.
Reserve the lower-left to lower-middle as a title-safe zone for two to four stacked white headline bands. Render the exact episode title in those bands as bold, readable black uppercase lettering.
Use black, cream, sepia, and restrained oxblood accents; keep the image sober, legible, and mobile-readable.
required_elements: two to four stacked white bands containing the exact episode title
avoid_elements: copied creator trade dress, logos, watermarks, channel names, or recognizable source-thumbnail layouts
unsupported secret plots, ethnic or religious scapegoating, a sole-cause claim, or claims of intentionality not supported by the episode's evidence
sensational accusations, conspiracy imagery, dense labels, illegible map text, placeholder lettering, or post-render headline overlays
more than one competing figure, excessive arrows, or a crowded undifferentiated collage
visual_style_guidance: Original archival editorial collage: high-contrast black-and-cream figure or artifact study, weathered parchment map, restrained sepia documentary texture, sparse oxblood route marks, and bold white newspaper-like headline bands. Preserve the selected project visual art style as the final rendering authority; do not imitate a specific channel or publisher.
